newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen up, continues recent gains.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen up, continues recent gains.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open higher Wednesday after rising yesterday on firm air-conditioning demand in the Southwest and outages of several generating units in the West.
"The timing was perfect. You have the hot weather and a couple of units out, while you were on the way up," said a Houston futures trader.

In over-the-counter business, July Palo Verde (PV) futures were quoted at $30.50-31.00 against Tuesday's settlement at $30.21 after traded as high as $32.25, while July California-Oregon Border (COB) was discussed at $20.25-20.75 higher than yesterday's close at $19.69.
July PV, in two days, gained $2.53 or 9.1 percent, while July COB rose $1.89 or 10.6 percent.
On the upside, analysts said July PV is expected to test chart resistance at $31.00 and $32.50 and July COB is expected to close a price gap at $20.25-20.70.

Salt River Project (SRP) said its 750 megawatt (MW) unit 3 at its Navajo coal-fired power plant near Page, Arizona, tripped off line early Tuesday, and was expected to ramp up to full power later in the days.
The market speculated over the operating status of the unit, but SRP did not confirm the trip until late Tuesday.
Moreover, all three Navajo units have been operating at half load over the past few days due to mild weather and weak demand for electricity, SRP said.
Pacific Gas & Electric Co said its Moss Landing natural gas-fired plant in Monterey, Calif., tripped off line late Monday, and expected to resume operation Wednesday afternoon.
The Moss Landing station on the central California coast has two units with a total capacity of 1,500 MW.
In other generation news, the 750 MW unit 1 at the Mohave coal-fired plant in Nevada was expected to return on line Tuesday following a Saturday shutdown for maintenance.
Startup of a 185 MW unit 1 at the Four Corners coal-fired plant in New Mexico was delayed to early today due to a boiler tube leak.
Also, the 1,112 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state and 1,087 MW San Onofre 3 nuclear unit in southern California were scheduled to resume output by next week.
The complex's rise has also been underpinned by concern over reduced Northwest power supplies to southern California this summer, market sources said.
A Western Systems Coordinating Council committee is expected to introduce a proposal later this week to derate the Pacific Intertie transmission system in early July.
The plan called for a summertime rating for the intertie at 6,900 MW from the current limit of 7,200 MW.
